sample_unit: emergency medicine patient records (50-summary subsample reviewed by 3 physicians)

links.outcome: Physician-rated safety and usefulness of LLM handoff notes versus physician-written notes, critical risks
links.effect: Mean safety 4.06 (0.86) vs 4.50 (0.56) for physician-written; usefulness 4.04 vs 4.36 out of 5; no LLM summary rated a critical patient safety risk.
links.quote: None of the LLM-generated summaries were classified as a critical patient safety risk.

unlisted_practices: Novel patient safety-focused physician-rated framework (readability, completeness, curation, correctness, usefulness, safety) for preimplementation evaluation of LLM handoff notes
Comparison of automated metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore, SCALE) against physician review

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and testing an LLM pipeline to generate emergency medicine handoff notes using retrospective EHR data and clinician grading of safety and accuracy, but it does not compare outcomes with vs without an organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
